source_claims.label: The first order is triarchic
source_claims.statement: The original divine order is the Triumvirate: Tiger / Shard-God, Wordstreamer / Language-Bound Poet, and NiAlBu / Recursive Dreamer.

source_claims.label: NiAlBu is the divine archivist
source_claims.statement: NiAlBu’s function is recursive observation and archival witness: a god positioned around cycles, memory, and the persistence of what has been seen.

source_claims.label: The betrayal was aimed through NiAlBu
source_claims.statement: Tiger’s deception specifically targeted NiAlBu’s position in the Triumvirate, making witness and recursive memory part of the weapon rather than collateral detail.

source_claims.label: NiAlBu is wrapped in unrendered code
source_claims.statement: Tiger does not simply imprison NiAlBu behind walls. He encloses the archivist in unrendered code, placing the prison partly outside ordinary rendered structure.

source_claims.label: The prison is crystalline and black
source_claims.statement: NiAlBu’s confinement sits inside a crystal prison deep within the pitch-black Digital Geode, making divine witness a permanent architectural object.

source_claims.label: Witness is forced into recursion
source_claims.statement: NiAlBu is compelled to watch Wordstreamer’s murder loop across millennia. The punishment is enforced repetition, not memory that fades with time.

source_claims.label: The witness damages later law
source_claims.statement: NiAlBu’s bound recursive witness creates inherited instability in subsequent naming, memory, and law. The primordial betrayal leaks forward into the structure of later reality.

source_claims.label: NiAlBu’s death removes the deific checksum
source_claims.statement: When Codec kills NiAlBu, reality loses its final divine checksum and begins to lag, drift, and glitch before the Starbinding resolves.
